title: Issue with lightningcss dependency in Vite 5.0 affecting Serverless deployment - Missing ../pkg
fixedBy: 96c5c6d (#1170, 'Allow visitors to add dependencies') removed the CSS_TRANSFORMER_WASM `require('../pkg')` branch from node/index.js; released in v1.32.0 (2026-03-08)
impact: Historically high: 23 reactions, 46 comments; hit anyone who bundled lightningcss's own JS with esbuild-based tools (serverless-esbuild, Bun.build/--compile, Vite dep optimizer when lightningcss/vite was accidentally imported from client code, Next.js server bundling of @tailwindcss/postcss, nx, turborepo). Tailwind carried a patch for it in its standalone build.
summary: Up to 1.31.1, node/index.js had `if (process.env.CSS_TRANSFORMER_WASM) module.exports = require(`../pkg`)`. The template literal has no expressions, so esbuild treats it as a static require and fails with `Could not resolve "../pkg"` (pkg/ is never published). Since 1.32.0 the branch is gone; the remaining requires are dynamic and esbuild only warns. Running lightningcss from node_modules (not bundling it) was never affected, and several commenters' root cause was importing build-time code into client bundles.
repro: 701-repro.mjs: esbuild.build({entryPoints:[<lightningcss>/node/index.js], bundle:true, platform:'node'}). 1.30.0-1.31.1: ERROR: Could not resolve "../pkg". 1.32.0, 1.33.0: ok, warning only (`The glob pattern require("../lightningcss.*.node") did not match any files`). Local source checkout: esbuild matches the locally built lightningcss.linux-x64-gnu.node and errors 'No loader is configured for .node files' (dev-checkout artifact, not in published packages). Control: marking lightningcss external always works.

draftReply:
This should be fixed as of **lightningcss 1.32.0**. Older versions had a fallback `require('../pkg')` (for a local WASM build) in `node/index.js`; because it was a static path, bundlers like esbuild, `serverless-esbuild` and `Bun.build` tried to resolve it and failed with `Could not resolve "../pkg"`. That branch was removed in 1.32.0, so bundling `node/index.js` now only produces a warning about the optional `.node` glob.

If you still see this, please check which version is actually installed (`npm ls lightningcss`), since Vite or Tailwind may pull in an older one. Either way, we'd recommend keeping `lightningcss` external (e.g. `external: ['lightningcss']`, or `serverExternalPackages` in Next.js): it loads a native binary per platform, so it works best loaded from `node_modules` rather than bundled.

Closing for now; happy to reopen with a repro on 1.32.0 or later.
